messages:
maria_ng: Heads-up — overnight perf alert from the nightly dashboard: 95th tail latency up ~3x and throughput down ~18% starting around 01:12 UTC. Looks correlated with last night's mergesweep (merge queue sweep).
chris_k: saw that, thanks. Any obvious correlation with kernel-selector changes?
zoe_r: quick glance at the merge list: PR #5924 (batcher heuristic tweak) and #5931 (prober scheduling cleanup) landed around that window.
dave_l: perf-bot posted a CI regression for the prober e2e at 01:05 too — linking logs.
perf-bot: CI / e2e | prober_concurrency_test FAILED (latency regression) — job: prober-e2e-nightly-420 — artifacts: https://ci.redwood/prober-e2e/420/artifacts
maria_ng: can someone grab a few flamegraphs from the affected hosts? prefer host: runtime-prod-phi-12 where the spike is largest.
chris_k: pulling profiles now. cmd: ssh prod@runtime-prod-phi-12 sudo /opt/redwood/bin/collect-profile --pid=$(pgrep runtime) --duration=30s --out=/tmp/prof-fold.tar.gz
chris_k: uploaded /tmp/prof-fold.tar.gz to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/nightly/1739991111/prof-fold.tar.gz
zoe_r: quick diff of the two PRs — #5924 lowered the batch-merge threshold from 32->24 for mem-bound queues; #5931 changed the prober to prefer small batches for short seqs. both could interact badly.
dave_l: looking at the flamegraph: a big chunk (~60%) of time is in batcher.internal::wait_for_fill (queueing), and kernel-selector spin path shows increased context switches.
maria_ng: that screams batch fragmentation — fewer requests per batch so kernel overhead per token up. any KV-cache misses changed?
chris_k: KV miss rate spiked 4x in the same timeframe, from 2.1%->8.6% on phi-12. logs: "kv_cache: miss key prefix_len=64" repeated.
zoe_r: interesting — prober small-batches means more unique prefixes hitting the cache before warm, could increase eviction churn.
dave_l: can we repro locally with synthetic probe load? I'll run prober-e2e with old vs new heuristics.
maria_ng: run with load profile: mix of short (seq<=32) and long (seq>=256) at 60/40, concurrency 240, use --kv-stats flag.
dave_l: started runs. initial results mirror production: new heuristics -> avg batch size down 1.9x, KV miss up 3.7x, tail latency up 2.8x. old heuristics good.
chris_k: ok, sounds like #5931 is the likely trigger but the interaction with #5924 amplifies it. propose revert #5931 immediately and then revert or tweak #5924 in follow-up.
zoe_r: agree. we should also add a canary test that probes mix-of-lengths to detect this class of regression.
maria_ng: @ops please hold the rollout for the mergesweep until we revert. ops?
perf-bot: Deploy blocker label applied to release/mergesweep by maria_ng at 01:45 UTC
ops (auto): Hold placed on mergesweep rollout — awaiting revert or mitigation.
dave_l: opened revert PR #5948 to back out the prober scheduling cleanup, requesting urgent review.
chris_k: while revert lands, temp mitigation: bump batch-merge threshold back to 32 via a hotfix config, and enable aggressive KV prefetch for short sequences on prod-phi.
zoe_r: I can prepare the hotfix patch. will also add a short-term metric alert for batch-size drop < 60% of baseline.
maria_ng: thanks. after revert+hotfix we should run an extended nightly (2h) smoke on phi to validate. add a checklist in the revert PR describing perf checks.
dave_l: revert merged and hotfix config pushed to phi-12 at 02:12 UTC, rolling to the cluster.
perf-bot: Monitoring: 10m after hotfix, 95th tail latency back within 10% of baseline, throughput recovered to -2% of baseline.
chris_k: filing a postmortem entry — root cause: prober scheduling change increased small-batch preference causing batch fragmentation and KV-cache churn, amplified by a concurrent batch-merge threshold tweak.
zoe_r: action items: 1) stricter canary tests (mix-length probe), 2) add synthetic KV-warmup for new scheduling, 3) revert + incremental rollout process docs.
maria_ng: nice work triaging quickly. please keep the deploy blocker until overnight run completes. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
